editorial:
You follow Alex Honnold as he prepares to climb Yosemite's El Capitan without ropes or safety gear. The film shows his calm personality, his relationship, and the huge risk he takes. It feels tense and personal, like watching someone chase a dream that could end badly. The camera work puts you right on the wall and makes every move feel huge. You also see the people around him worry, which adds real emotion and keeps the story grounded.

The climbing scenes are amazing, and the pacing keeps you nervous from start to finish. It is inspiring but also scary, and some moments feel slow when the film focuses on prep and daily life. If you like real-life adventure, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound. The ending is unforgettable and worth the wait. It is not for everyone, especially if heights make you nervous.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alex starts the climb at dawn and moves up the wall with no ropes. After hours of careful climbing, he reaches the top of El Capitan and finishes the route. He celebrates quietly, then calls his girlfriend to tell her he made it. The film ends with him standing on the summit, safe and proud, after completing the historic climb.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real-life adventure and climbing stories.
